anya: Quick dump from this morning's bring-up: ran confidence-rolloff + speculative soft-handoff on nova-13b-quant to see where chunk-overlap helps. Short summary: throughput ~1.6x with overlap=128 but a measurable drop on long-answer F1 for open-domain QA.

devin: can you share the exact run flags and one counterexample?

anya: repro command below. key knobs: overlap=0/64/128, early_rolloff=0.7/0.85, min_emit=2, lut_mode=calibrated/v1.
```
bench_spec --model nova-13b-q --dataset odqa-long --n 600 --overlap 128 --early_rolloff 0.85 --min_emit 2 --lut calibrated
```

sora: what do you mean by "calibrated" lut mode? is that the soft-bias correction from the quant team?

anya: yes 1% soft-bias correction applied to high-freq logits (per-token shift), intended to preserve tail mass. without it we saw more generic short endings.

devin: interesting. numbers?

anya: baseline (no spec): F1=72.8, P95 latency=210ms. spec+overlap=128+calibrated-lut: F1=71.0, throughput 1.6x, median latency down ~45%. spec+overlap=0 (no overlap) had F1=68.9 with many truncation cases.

sora: so overlap helps but doesn't fully close gap. do we have per-token entropy traces to see where exits occur?

anya: yes attached in artefact. pattern: exits spike right after chunk boundary when entropy drops below threshold. calibrated-lut reduces spike magnitude but doesn't eliminate it. also saw a handful of cases where min_emit=2 prevented truncation.

devin: can we try adaptive edge-threshold: raise early_rolloff by +0.12 on tokens within 20 tokens of a chunk edge? might prevent premature exit while keeping perf.

anya: good idea. i'll run an adaptive-edge sweep: early_rolloff base [0.7,0.8], edge_delta [+0.08,+0.12], overlap [64,128], min_emit [2,4]. will capture NLL trajectories and exact-match diffs for a 500-sample subset.
